question: What is the primary purpose of the Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in healthcare facilities?

options.A: To generate excessive profit for hospital management
options.B: To ensure a continuous and uninterrupted supply of essential drugs
options.C: To replace the need for government healthcare budgets entirely
options.D: To provide free medications to all citizens without any payment

explanation: The DRF is a self-sustaining mechanism designed primarily to ensure that essential drugs are continuously available and do not run out due to funding delays. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h1)

question: How does the revolving cycle of the DRF function financially?

options.A: Funds from drug sales are used to repurchase and replenish stock
options.B: Revenue generated is sent directly to the federal treasury without returns
options.C: Donations from international bodies fund every subsequent drug purchase
options.D: Patients pay taxes on hospital admissions to fund the drugs

explanation: The DRF operates on a cycle where money collected from selling drugs is directly used to procure more inventory, keeping the supply chain active. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h1)

question: What major healthcare issue does the DRF aim to eliminate in public facilities?
explanation: The DRF directly targets and works to eliminate the out-of-stock syndrome, ensuring medications are always accessible when prescribed. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why is financial self-reliance through the DRF important for healthcare institutions in Nigeria?

options.A: It allows facilities to bypass government budgetary delays and maintain stock
options.B: It eliminates the need for any clinical documentation
options.C: It permits nurses to prescribe independent surgical procedures
options.D: It ensures that healthcare workers receive tax-free salaries

explanation: Self-reliance allows facilities to avoid dependence on delayed or insufficient government budget releases for purchasing pharmaceutical supplies. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is a primary danger of diverting DRF revenue to pay for non-drug hospital expenses?

options.A: It causes immediate nursing staff shortages
options.B: It breaks the revolving cycle and leads to system collapse
options.C: It increases the expiration rate of surgical instruments
options.D: It forces NAFDAC to withdraw hospital licenses

explanation: Diverting funds means money needed to repurchase drugs is missing, which breaks the revolving cycle and causes the drug supply system to fail. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why must drugs procured under the DRF meet standards set by regulatory bodies like NAFDAC?

options.A: To guarantee drug quality and safety for the patients
options.B: To ensure the hospital receives international grants
options.C: To allow nurses to prescribe medications independently
options.D: To increase the profit margin of the pharmacy department

explanation: Regulatory bodies like NAFDAC ensure that all drugs procured are safe, effective, and of high quality for patient consumption. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h3)

question: What role do nurses play in drug demand estimation at the ward level?

options.A: They manufacture generic tablets for the hospital
options.B: They track daily patient utilization patterns to prevent overstocking or understocking
options.C: They set the market prices for imported pharmaceuticals
options.D: They audit the personal bank accounts of the hospital accountants

explanation: Nurses track daily patient utilization in their units, helping determine accurate requisitions that prevent stock imbalances. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why is the proper maintenance of ward emergency trolleys by nurses important for the DRF?

options.A: It ensures that emergency drugs are safely stored and accounted for
options.B: It generates immediate cash revenue from emergency admissions
options.C: It replaces the need for a central pharmacy department
options.D: It allows nurses to sell medications for personal profit

explanation: Properly managed emergency trolleys ensure drugs are safe, unexpired, well-accounted for, and ready for immediate clinical use. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h4)

question: What does the acronym FEFO stand for in inventory control and stock monitoring?
explanation: FEFO stands for First-Expiry, First-Out, an essential inventory management rule ensuring older stocks close to expiration are used first. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h5)

question: How can nurses help prevent pharmaceutical waste caused by drug expiration in wards?

options.A: By returning near-expiry drugs to the manufacturer for cash refunds
options.B: By identifying near-expiry items early and ensuring they are used or redistributed promptly
options.C: By altering the expiration dates printed on the drug packaging
options.D: By administering double doses to patients to finish the stock faster

explanation: Early identification and prompt utilization or redistribution of near-expiry medications prevent them from expiring on the shelves and causing financial loss. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of rational drug use in healthcare settings?

options.A: To maximize the financial profit of the pharmacy unit
options.B: To ensure patients receive appropriate medications matching their clinical needs at the lowest cost
options.C: To encourage the prescription of as many brand-name drugs as possible
options.D: To eliminate the need for physician consultations

explanation: Rational drug use focuses on appropriate clinical matching, proper dosages, adequate duration, and cost-effectiveness for the patient. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h6)

question: How do nurses directly support patient safety regarding DRF-purchased medications?

options.A: By strictly adhering to the rights of medication administration
options.B: By purchasing bulk medications directly from international markets
options.C: By setting the retail prices for emergency drugs in the ward
options.D: By replacing expired drugs with herbal remedies

explanation: Following the rights of medication administration ensures that patients receive the exact correct drug safely, avoiding adverse errors. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h6)

question: Why is strict revenue collection and prompt banking essential for the DRF?

options.A: It allows nurses to receive direct performance bonuses
options.B: It maintains continuous cash flow needed for immediate inventory replenishment
options.C: It removes the need for annual hospital financial audits
options.D: It guarantees free healthcare services for all hospital staff

explanation: Continuous cash flow from prompt revenue collection and banking is necessary to buy replacement stock and keep the DRF revolving. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h7)

question: What should a nurse do when handling cash collections for DRF drugs in a ward setting?

options.A: Keep the cash in a secure personal pocket until the end of the month
options.B: Use the money to purchase snacks or refreshments for the night shift
options.C: Ensure proper receipting and prompt deposit into designated DRF accounts
options.D: Lend the money to colleagues facing financial emergencies

explanation: Proper receipting and prompt deposition into official DRF accounts ensure transparency and protect against financial misappropriation. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is a major consequence of inflation and currency devaluation on the DRF system?

options.A: It increases the number of qualified nursing personnel
options.B: It causes capital erosion, making it harder to purchase the same volume of drugs
options.C: It automatically eliminates all forms of medication wastage
options.D: It forces pharmaceutical companies to give drugs away for free

explanation: Inflation and currency devaluation erode the purchasing power of the fixed DRF capital, resulting in fewer drugs being able to be repurchased. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h8)

question: How can healthcare facilities best mitigate the challenge of patient credit and uncollected debts in the DRF?

options.A: By strictly enforcing credit policies and minimizing bad debt accumulation
options.B: By stopping all drug sales to emergency patients permanently
options.C: By charging nurses personally for any unpaid patient bills
options.D: By increasing the prices of drugs tenfold to cover all losses

explanation: Enforcing clear credit policies prevents the accumulation of uncollected debts that drain the revolving capital of the DRF. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h8)
